significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish that "a reference model sharing the teacher's base" detects hidden trait content and that detection AUC declines with reference-model divergence "in tandem with transmission strength." This is a form-(iii) predictive coupling among measurable divergence, detectability, and transmission—not merely an existence claim—and would establish both a useful phenomenon and evidence for a shared-init mechanism, fixing expectations for unseen reference checkpoints and detector selection. The Cloud et al. (2025) subliminal-learning work located in search reports both shared-base dependence of transmission and poor detection by humans and generic classifiers, so the proposed coupling bears directly on a load-bearing explanation; a verified-false result would instead rule out the claim that transmission-enabling geometry is correspondingly readable by a same-base auditor, although it would not by itself identify another mechanism. True and false are distinguishable despite the unspecified functional form, and the topic-substitution check does not preserve this score: generic research on subliminal learning would not imply the specific detectability–divergence law.

reach.justification: The named handle is "an auditor" using a "same-base reference" to produce gradient-alignment or activation-probe scores and flag trait-laden corpora with high AUC. It is ex ante because it can screen a candidate distillation corpus before that corpus is used, giving pipeline operators an opportunity to reject, investigate, or gate the data rather than merely explaining an observed transfer afterward. After per-model re-extraction, the asserted "degradation law" still predicts that detection should fall with reference divergence and track transmission strength, so part of the conclusion transfers as a relation rather than only as a recipe for searching. Its scope is synthetic-data and distillation settings where the base or a close approximation is available, with auditors and model-pipeline operators downstream; the topic-substitution check lowers generic subliminal-learning research to the median, whereas this specific pre-training audit handle plus transferable coupling supports the higher score.
